summary: Replace the escalation arm's wall-clock teardown ceiling with the event-based read of the tick's own announce line

per.section: The default test lane must stay fast

acceptance: The ignores-SIGTERM case holds no wall-clock comparison; "the declared grace timed this, not the default" is read off the tick's announce line, and nothing in the arm is sized for a quiet host.
notes: Two records claim this: the inbox flake finding and the ONE-STATE-ROOT-LISTING-PROVES-ITS-ABSENCE note, whose entry a 4141ms teardown reverted against the 2500ms ceiling (case alone: 1436ms). The sibling case already reads `signalled; waiting for <n>ms (supervisorPolicy.killGraceMs)`. A wider or tighter number is not the fix — the cited section rules the assertion event-based. Whole diff is the file holding the case, so no tests[] line is judgeable.

summary: Seed the spawn scan from a test-helper's names that reach a process start, so a file spawning only via makeFixture declares the lane's budget

per.section: The default test lane must stay fast

acceptance: The scan reports tests/loopSupervisor.test.ts as a spawning file carrying no file-scope budget, that file declares the budget, and the default lane is green.
tests: the spawn scan names a lane file whose only process start is reached through a test-helper import
notes: `reachingNames` is per-SourceFile, so `makeFixture` (tests/helpers/dispatcherFixture.ts, which calls `exec`) is invisible and tests/loopSupervisor.test.ts inherits vitest's 5s default — it timed out there beside a wave, reverting CITATION-VERDICTS-NAME-THEIR-SITES-IN-THE-FIRST-LINE. The carve-out the file declares is for TIMERS (`waitFor`), not for process starts. Measured: that is the only default-lane file the widening newly names.
